caseno: Criminal Petition For leave to appeal No. 543 of 2007.
lawyer:
Abdur Razzaq, Senior Advocate instructed by AKM Shahidul Huq Advocate-on-Record ------- For the Petitioner. 
Sufia Khatun, Advocate-on-Record ------- For Respondent No. 1 
Zahirul Islam, Advocate-on-Record ------- For Respondent No.2.
parties:
Bangladesh Co-operative Book Society Ltd ------- Appellant.
Vs.
Md Dastagirul Huq and another -------- Respondents
full_judgment:
Md Abdul Matin J: This petition for leave to appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 8-11-2007 passed by the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 11130 of 2007 filed under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure discharging the Rule. 

 2. The facts, in short, are that the petitioner filed the aforesaid Criminal Miscellaneous Case under section 561 A of the Code of Criminal Procedure challenging the judgment and order dated 19-7-2007 passed by the Metropolitan Sessions Judge, Chittagong in Criminal Revision No. 194 of 2007 allowing the revisional application and setting aside the order dated 15-7-2007 passed by the Metropolitan Magistrate, Chittagong giving appointment of receiver under section 146 of the Code of Criminal Procedure in Miscellaneous Case No. 207 of 2007 now pending before the said court of Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Chittagong. 

 3. In the Criminal Miscellaneous Case it was stated that the petitioner Bangladesh Co-Operative Book Society Ltd having its Head Office at Chittagong is owner of the disputed Shop No.9 situated at Niaz Monzil, 922, Jubilee Road, Kotwali, Chittagong. The respondent-opposite party No. I Md Dastagirul Haq was an unlawful occupant of the case shop and was a well-known terrorist in Chittagong. It was also stated that in the year 1975 the Book Society rented the case shop to one Mr Abdul Jalil, son of Md Muslim Ali of 16 Alauddin Colony, District-Chittagong. The father of the opposite party No.1 (i.e. respondent No.1 of the Leave Petition) was merely a business partner of Mr Abdul Jail. But the respondent-opposite party No. 1 is neither a tenant nor a licensee of the shop rather he had been trying to forcefully occupy the shop No.9 without any approval from the Book Society. 

 4. It was further stated on behalf of the petitioner that on 21st June 2007 at about 9-30 PM the respondent-opposite Party No. 1 with other 7/8 local terrorists trespassed into the case shop by breaking the collapsible gate and shutter gate of the shop. They demolished part of the shop and dug a three foot big hole to change the structure of the case shop. They took away the collapsible gate and shutter gate of the shop. They caused huge losses and damages to the Book Society. It was Thursday night and, as such, the officers of the Book Society were not aware about the incident and could not take any immediate step to stop the opposite party No. 1 from the trespass, theft and damages. The security guards and Ansars of the Niaz Monzil tried to resist them but could not succeed. The respondent-opposite party No. 1 and the other terrorists threatened the security guards and the Ansars to kill them and tried to snatch their arms. 

 5. It was contended by the petitioner that on 23rd June 2007 it filed complaints against the respondent-opposite party No. 1 before the Kotwali Police Station and subsequently on 25th June 2007 before the Court of Chief Metropolitan Magistrate (CMM), Chittagong. The learned CMM thereafter ordered the Kotwali Police Station to investigate into the matter and treat the complaint as FIR if the prima facie case was made out. The respondent- opposite party No. 1 thereafter threatened the officers and staffs of the Book Society to withdraw the complaint. On 26th June 2007 at about 7-00 PM he with other 10/12 hired terrorists came to Niaz Monzil for taking revenge against the staffs of the Book Society and at one stage they tried to break into the case shop and tried to take forceful possession in it. On the same date the Book Society thereafter filed a General Diary in this regard and applied to the Kotwali Police Station for ensuring peace and law and order in the area. The Kotwali Police Station thereafter ordered to maintain status- quo in the case shop. 

 6. Subsequently, the Book Society filed an application before the CMM Chittagong for drawing up a proceeding under section 145 of the Code of Criminal Procedure in the case shop. The application was registered as Miscellaneous Case No. 207 of 2007. Thereafter a show cause notice was issued on the respondent-opposite party No. 1 and simultaneously the officer-in-charge of Kotwali PS was directed to submit an inquiry report in this regard. Thereafter again on 28th June and 30th June 2007 respondent-opposite party No. 1 with the help of other terrorists violated the order of CMM threatened the Manager and other staffs of the Book Society to withdraw the case. In this respect, the Book Society lodged a general diary. Thereafter following an application of the Book Society on 1st July 2007 the learned CMM, Chittagong directed the OC of Kotwali PS to maintain peace and tranquillity and take lawful action in this regard. 

 8. It was further stated for the petitioner that since the respondent-opposite party kept interfering with the peaceful possession of the Book Society in the Niaz Monzil and in the case shop, on 11th July 2007 it applied before the CMM for an order under section 146 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for attachment of the case shop until the dispute regarding the shop is not settled and appoint the OC of Kotwali PS as receiver of the shop. The application was heard on 15th July 2007 and after considering the facts and circumstances and the police report dated 8-7-2007 the learned CMM, Chittagong passed an order under section 146 of the Code of Criminal Procedure to appoint the officer-in-Charge of Kotwali Police Station as receiver for the case shop. Thereafter, on 18th July 2007 the respondent- opposite party No. 1 filed an application before the CMM to stay operation of the order of appointment of receiver, but the said application was rejected. 

 9. It was also contended for the petitioner on 19th July 2007 the respondent-opposite party No. 1 filed a Criminal Revision being No. 194 of 2007 under sections 435/439A of the Code of Criminal Procedure to challenge the order of appointment of receiver dated 15th July 2007 before the learned District and Sessions Judge, Chittagong. He prayed for calling for the record of Miscellaneous Case No. 2070f2007. On the same date the revisional application was moved before the learned District Sessions Judge, Chittagong for admission. The learned Advocate of the Book Society was occasionally present at the time of the admission hearing of the Criminal Revision in the same court in a different matter. He opposed the application and prayed for an adjournment so that he could inform the Book Society about the Criminal Revision and submit his Vokalatnama and written objection on its behalf. The learned Sessions Judge did not consider the application for adjournment and instantly admitted and allowed the Criminal Revision without giving any notice to the Book Society. 

 10. Upon preliminary bearing of the said Criminal Miscellaneous Case on 30th July 2007 a Division Bench of the High Court Division issued a Rule as per prayer made in the Criminal Miscellaneous Case. The High Court Division had also stayed operation of the impugned order of the learned Metropolitan Sessions Judge, Chittagong dated 19th July 2007 in Criminal Revision No. 194 of 2007. 

 11. The respondent-opposite party No. 1 contested the Rule by filling affidavit-in-opposition. It was stated by the respondent-opposite party No. 1 that he was not an unlawful occupant of the case shop in question. His father, Nurul Haq had been in possession of the shop as monthly tenant from the year 1978 and since then he was in possession having a business establishment. After his death, the respondent-opposite party No.1 being his son, continued tenancy in the shop and carried on business in the shop by paying regular rent to the landlord- society. The respondent-opposite party No.1 stated that the petitioner intentionally filed series of cases against him only for unnecessary harassment and to create pressure upon him for vacating the shop. 

 12. It was also contended by the respondent- opposite party No. 1 that the petitioner admitted that the respondent-opposite party No.1 had been in possession of the disputed shop. The respondent- opposite party also stated that when the Book Society filed the application under section 145 of the Code of Criminal Procedure in Miscellaneous Case No. 207 of 2007 the learned Magistrate was not satisfied as to the apprehension of breach of peace. As such the learned CMM issued a show cause notice on the respondent-opposite party No. 1 in this regard fixing the next dated as on 9-8-2007 for order. The opposite party also contends that the police report dated 8-7-2007 was uncalled for and totally false. 

 13. The respondent-opposite party No. 1 further stated that although the case was fixed on 9-8-2007 for submitting reply of the show cause notice, the petitioner again submitted an application on 11-7-2007 under section 146 of the Code of Criminal Procedure stating some false allegations against the respondent-opposite party No.1. On 15-7-2007 the application was heard without serving any show cause notice and behind the back and knowledge of the respondent-opposite party No. 1. The learned CMM thereafter passed an order for appointment of receiver for the case shop under section 146 of the Code of Criminal Procedure behind the back and knowledge of the respondent-opposite party No.1. It was also stated that the petitioner obtained the order by playing fraud upon the learned Magistrate. 

 14. It was further stated for the respondent- opposite party No. 1 that there was no ingredient of section 146 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, since the respondent-opposite party No.1 admittedly was in possession of the case shop as a tenant under the petitioner. The Officer-in-Charge also took possession of the shop from the possession of the respondent-opposite party No. 1 after preparing a seizure list of the goods found in the shop. On 19-9-2007 the Book Society served a legal notice on the respondent-opposite party No.1 giving opportunity to surrender the tenancy within 31-10-2007. It was further stated that there were various items of cloths in the shop and the same would be damaged and there was also no provision for attachment of the property when the respondent-opposite party No. 1 had been running the shop. 

 15. The Criminal Miscellaneous case was heard by a Division of the High Court Division. At the hearing of the said criminal miscellaneous case it was submitted on behalf of the petitioner that the learned Sessions Judge did not call for the record of Miscellaneous Case No. 207 of 2007 before allowing the criminal revision as required under section 439A of the Code of Criminal Procedure and, as such, the learned Sessions Judge in passing the order dated 19th July 2007 acted unlawfully and without jurisdiction and the same order should be declared as illegal and void to secure ends of justice. It was also argued that the impugned order was an abuse of process of the Court since the learned Sessions Judge acted without lawful authority inasmuch as he allowed the Criminal Revision without giving any show cause notice to the petitioner herein. It was further submitted on behalf of the petitioner that the impugned order violated the principle of natural justice, inasmuch as the petitioner herein was not given any chance to defend the criminal revision before it was allowed to his detriment. 

 16. It was further submitted for the petitioner that he is owner of the disputed shop and the respondent-opposite party No.1 had destroyed part of the shop and had been trying to cause further damages to the case shop. The order of appointment of receiver dated 15th July 2007 had stopped the respondent-opposite party No. 1 from demolishing the shop any further. But the impugned order of cancelling the order of appointment of receiver gave the respondent-opposite party No. 1 an opportunity to cause further damages to the case shop. More- over, the learned Sessions Judge had directed the CMM, Chittagong to decide the matter of appointment of receiver on the next date of the Miscellaneous Case No. 207 of 2007 i.e. on 9th August 2007. If the impugned order was not stayed the opposite party No. 1 would have destroyed the case shop and made necessary change to the shop before the dispute regarding possession of the land was resolved. 

 17. On the other hand, it was submitted on behalf of the respondent-opposite party No. 1 that the petitioner without serving any notice, managed to obtain the impugned order dated 15-7-2007 for appointment of receiver with respect to the disputed shop by suppressing facts. It was also argued on behalf of the opposite party No. 1 that there was no ingredient of section 146 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for appointment of the receiver for the case shop which had been in possession of the respondent-opposite party No. 1 for long time. There was no material before the learned CMM to pass such an order in an off date. 

 19. After hearing both sided on 8th November 2007 the High Court Division discharged the Rule and thereby upheld the judgment and order dated 19-7-2007 passed by the Metropolitan Sessions Judge, Chittagong in Criminal Revision No. 194 of 2007 admitting and allowing the revisional application and cancelling the order dated 15-7-2007 for appointment of receiver under section 146 of the Code of Criminal Procedure passed by the learned Metropolitan Magistrate, Chittagong in Miscellaneous Case No. 207 of 2007. 

 23. Order under section 146 could have been passed only after being satisfied on evidence in the proceeding under section 145 of the Code of Criminal Procedure that neither party could prove his possession in the subject matter of the proceeding and therefore the order passed by the learned magistrate was misconceived and beyond the authority under section 146 of the Code of Criminal Procedure.
